observations.epoch_band_state_and_other_notes: J1634+44 is catalogued here as a white-dwarf-hosting LPT candidate. Bloot+25 report ILT J163430+445010 with 19 LOFAR pulses, duration <=10 s, pulse period 841.24808 +/- 0.00015 s, maximum Stokes V flux density 383 +/- 52 mJy, DM=22.5 +/- 5.5 pc cm^-3, distance 1.0-4.3 kpc, and a marginal UV/optical counterpart suggestive of a 15000-33000 K white dwarf. They propose possible spin-orbit resonance with a companion period of 2103.110 s or 1402 s, but this is not entered as P_orb. Dong+25 report CHIME J1634+44, VLA localization, 841 s pulses, a secondary 4206 s bursting pattern, peak flux about 0.4-9 Jy in CHIME/Pulsar data, and 0.3-10 keV Swift/XRT upper limits; no confirmed Gaia DR3 counterpart is available. Audit correction: Bloot+25 Table 2 identifies the 383 +/- 52 mJy 2016-05-19 value as Stokes I and gives Stokes V=-346 +/- 33 mJy; Table 1 note conflicts by calling 383 +/- 52 mJy Stokes V. Retain detailed Table 2 identification and flag CHIME1634-005. Later detections extend from 110 MHz to 3 GHz; frequencies, observing states and fluxes remain separate in rawdog_measurements.csv. The LOFAR and VLA positions differ by 3.53 arcsec; optical/UV associations remain unresolved, and no Gaia ID is assigned.

issues.competing_evidence: Bloot+25 LOFAR position is 16:34:30 +44:50:10 (±2 arcsec, stated 3 sigma); its GALEX FUV candidate is 0.57 arcsec away and UNIONS detections are nearby. Dong+25 VLA position is 16:34:29.96 +44:50:13.5 (reported 1-sigma upper uncertainties 0.5 and 1.1 arcsec), about 3.53 arcsec from the LOFAR position. The FUV candidate is about 4.08 arcsec from the VLA center. Dong+25 HSC source lies outside 2 sigma but within 3 sigma, is classified extended, has 5.8% chance alignment, and lacks GALEX UV detection. A 0.46 arcsec/yr scale over the 2016–2023 interval is within Bloot+25’s <1 arcsec/yr limit, but no proper motion is measured. Gaia DR3 query finds no source inside 18.006 arcsec.
issues.why_it_matters: Association of the optical/UV candidate determines whether the WD evidence can be used and whether any Gaia/CMD information belongs to this system.
issues.needed_action: Keep Gaia ID unassigned. Obtain high-resolution, multi-epoch astrometry and deeper UV/optical imaging/spectroscopy tied to the VLA position; determine whether the GALEX/UNIONS and HSC sources are the same object and whether either is physically associated.

issues.competing_evidence: Bloot+25 argues for a WD-containing system from marginal GALEX/UNIONS photometry and a conditional WD SED fit. Dong+25 finds the HSC source potentially extended with 5.8% chance alignment, no GALEX UV detection, and argues the high circular polarization, radio energy and microstructure are more pulsar-like; active magnetars are constrained by X-rays but NS-like alternatives remain.
issues.why_it_matters: Classification affects whether this source belongs in a WD-hosting subset and any comparison with CVs or WD pulsars.
issues.needed_action: Retain LPT as confirmed and WD host as candidate. Seek secure optical/UV counterpart, spectroscopy, parallax, or other component-specific evidence before promoting the WD classification.

issues.competing_evidence: Bloot+25 measures an 841.24808 s pulse clock, a 4206.2406 s alternative interpulse timing solution, and proposes 2103.1061–2103.1141 s or 1402.0814–1402.0853 s orbital periods in 5:2/5:3 models. Dong+25 measures 841.245895 s with a significant negative derivative and a ~4206 s burst-arrival pattern, but states there is no evidence for the specific 2103 s orbit. Zhan+26 instead treats 841 s as orbit and 4206 s as spin-orbit beat in a double-WD model.
issues.why_it_matters: Confusing spin, orbital, beat, interpulse and burst-recurrence clocks would create a false Porb or evolutionary interpretation.
issues.needed_action: Keep all clocks separate and Porb unset. Confirm with a phase-coherent secondary-clock measurement, optical spectroscopy/eclipses, or independently measured orbital motion.

issues.competing_evidence: Bloot+25 DM=22.5±5.5 pc cm−3 gives 1.0–1.6 kpc with NE2001 and 1.5–4.3 kpc with YMW16. Dong+25 mean DM=25.0±0.2 gives 1.4 and 3.0 kpc with the same respective models. No Gaia parallax or independent distance is available.
issues.why_it_matters: Distance controls luminosity estimates and the conditional WD/companion SED solutions.
issues.needed_action: Keep model-specific estimates separate. Revise only after a secure counterpart and parallax, or a better calibrated distance method, is available.

issues.competing_evidence: Bloot+25 Table 1 lists 383±52 mJy and its note calls this Stokes V. Detailed Table 2 gives 383±52 mJy in Stokes I and −346±33 mJy in Stokes V for the 2016-05-19 pulse. The catalog value matches Table 2 Stokes I, not the Table 1 Stokes-V label.
issues.why_it_matters: A Stokes mislabel would distort polarization fraction and radio-flux comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Preserve both table values in the ledger and label the compatibility flux as Stokes I from Table 2; check for a published correction or author clarification before changing the adopted component.

issues.competing_evidence: Bloot+25 gives Teff=15,000–33,000 K and MWD≥0.78 Msun only if the marginal UV/optical detections are a homogeneous-surface WD SED; it quotes a lower distance bound >1.9 kpc. Dong+25 allows ~20,000–40,000 K only if the HSC source is real. Bloot+25 abstract/conclusion says earlier than M7 is ruled out, while §4.1 says M6 is excluded at 4.3 kpc and Figure 9 makes the limit distance dependent.
issues.why_it_matters: Treating these conditional fits or companion templates as measured component properties would overstate what the data establish.
issues.needed_action: Keep temperatures/mass as conditional model rows, not adopted direct values. Resolve counterpart identity and use Figure 9 with any justified distance before quoting a single companion spectral-type cutoff.

references.note: Discovery and WD-candidate interpretation for ILT J163430+445010. Reports 19 LOFAR pulses at 120–167 MHz, DM=22.5±5.5, 841.24808±0.00015 s pulse period, Pdot=−9±3e−12 s/s, alternative 4206.2406±0.0008 s interpulse model, and possible 5:2/5:3 resonance. GALEX/UNIONS photometry is marginal; WD Teff=15000–33000 K and MWD≥0.78 Msun are conditional on a genuine homogeneous WD counterpart. Important internal Stokes-label conflict: Table 1 note labels 383±52 mJy as Stokes V, while Table 2 gives Stokes I=383±52 and V=−346±33 mJy for the same pulse. LOFAR position is ~3.53 arcsec from later VLA position.
